pages.title: Making Money From
pages.summary: Making money from websites containing affiliate links is possible, but it is not as simple as publishing product round-ups and waiting for commissions. The basic model is straightforward: a website recommends a product or service, the reader clicks a tracked link, and the site owner earns a commission if that click leads to a qualifying purchase or action.

pages.title: Link Intent
pages.summary: Affiliate links work better when direct product links, written reviews, comparisons, and accessories match the viewer's stage of buying.

pages.title: Do Not Buy
pages.summary: Saying who should avoid a product can make affiliate content more useful and more believable.

pages.title: Overkill Picks
pages.summary: Readers trust a review more when it admits that a simpler or cheaper product is enough for some buyers.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Do Not Buy.

pages.title: Missing Features
pages.summary: A clear missing-feature warning helps readers avoid products that are cheap upfront but wrong for their routine.

pages.title: Review Rules
pages.summary: Regulators target fake and misleading reviews, so visible bad-fit advice can help affiliate pages look more independent.

pages.title: Risky Categories
pages.summary: In finance, health, childcare, electrical goods, and privacy tools, wrong recommendations can create more than inconvenience.

pages.title: Running Costs
pages.summary: Consumables, subscriptions, and locked ecosystems can turn a cheap product into the expensive choice over time.

pages.title: Workload Fit
pages.summary: A product can be well reviewed and still fail when the buyer's real workload is heavier than the review scenario.

pages.title: Wirecutter
pages.summary: Wirecutter shows how affiliate revenue can follow from rigorous testing, editorial standards, and reader trust.

pages.title: Separation
pages.summary: Wirecutter's model depends on readers believing that editors choose products before commissions enter the decision.

pages.title: Sub-Topic Index
pages.summary: Focused pages that expand on Wirecutter.

pages.title: Living Pages
pages.summary: A serious review page needs maintenance because stock, prices, models, warranties, and user complaints change after publication.

pages.title: Best Picks
pages.summary: Wirecutter's strongest pages reduce choice overload by making a clear recommendation and explaining the trade-offs behind it.

pages.title: Deal Filtering
pages.summary: Wirecutter's deal coverage shows that affiliate revenue can require heavy editorial filtering, not just adding sale links.

pages.title: Disclosure
pages.summary: Clear disclosure is only the legal floor; the harder job is making readers believe the ranking itself was not bought.

pages.title: Subscriptions
pages.summary: Wirecutter's move into subscriptions shows why even strong affiliate review brands may need revenue beyond commissions.
